submitted.rationale: All three measurements (indices 14, 26 and 0) read 0 A photocurrent, spanning the middle, Mg-rich end and Mn-rich end of the Mg–Mn line. Index 14 is a nominal choice because the three results are tied. It sits at the MgMn2O4 spinel composition, which MACE puts on the hull. MEGNet predicts a 2.87 eV gap for that spinel, below the 3.22 eV photon energy. The library appears photo-inactive under these conditions.

rejected.reason: Measured 0 A. Mn-rich region, where the predicted narrow gaps (Mn3O4 0.94 eV) likely mean strong recombination.

consultations.verdict: Support: MACE puts spinel MgMn2O4 on the hull (0 eV/atom), and MEGNet HSE gives a 2.87 eV gap, below the 3.22 eV photon energy, so it should absorb. Mg6MnO8 (3.74 eV) would be transparent. Index 14 (Mg 0.335) sits at the spinel stoichiometry.

Weak support: Mg3MnO4 is predicted at 2.24 eV (HSE), below the 3.22 eV photon energy, so Mg-rich rock-salt Mn-in-MgO phases should absorb. Mn3O4 (0.94 eV) is too narrow and likely lossy. The spinel point gave zero, so the Mg-rich end (index 26) is a different regime worth testing.

Mild support: MgMn6O12 (Mg 0.14) is predicted at 2.11 eV (HSE), so the Mn-rich end absorbs strongly at 3.22 eV. The middle and Mg-rich end both gave zero, so the Mn-rich end (index 0) is the only regime not yet tested.
